observations: Health is stored as one byte but general health arithmetic and HitPoints read it signed; shield arithmetic reads unsigned.
TakeDamage uses case-insensitive substring tokens and set=1..16 to scan active objects at stride0x10d8. All69 parsed authored combat uses execute in command fixtures.
SetHitPoints default is a sentinel fallback, not an unconditional reset token; a prior numeric value survives a later default token.
Invincibility is checked after entering the positive shield-damage branch; its flicker timer still resets even if the damage becomes0.
The original hit probe flag prevents the tested lethal effects but does not prevent nonlethal health mutation.
Incoming player hits can bypass an existing post-hit timer; NPC/null/inactive attacker paths differ.
Damage=-1 bypasses ordinary player invincibility in the bounded general-hit fixture and classifies as lethal.
Message values are loaded from the native record+0x28 before FTOL; Ghidra omitted that FPU load in the C listing.
With nonnull numeric parameter context, the native param substring branch passes the start of the word param into integer conversion; tested param0, param3 and prefixPaRaM99 all select slot0.
Currency deduction precedes cheat/timer suppression of the returned spawn quantity; suppression does not restore the deducted wallet value.
Heart-drop decisions use signed current-health bytes, unsigned maximum-health bytes and original QRAND; no-health cases do not advance RNG.
In one native command/hit/death sequence, SetHitPoints restored health after death but retained deathState=2; health assignment alone does not revive the NPC.

Kill was checked in all202authored uses, plus selection/token/weak-reference/NaN and embedded-NUL cases. x87 instructions reject unordered spawn timers in every checked branch; decompiler single-target >0 pseudocode is misleading.
limits: Full combat orchestration, special level/vehicle cases, populated AI/scripts, actual debris/pickup spawning and live feedback remain incomplete. Currency deduction and heart-drop decisions have bounded native checks.
The TakeDamage call site pushes six arguments; the trailing context1 argument is preserved by the adapter without claiming its meaning inside every callee.

The named-character resolver and final damage dispatch are fixture adapters in command suites. The message suite also intercepts only CRT sprintf for bounded %s formatting; original list lookup and numeric conversion execute.
Portable C# object classes project established fields; they do not reconstruct full original C++ class layouts.
Build success alone is not behavior equivalence.
